source_documents.title: Structural Engineering of Cyanine Dyes to Access Shortwave Infrared-Emissive J-Aggregates

reference_evidence_units.quote: We hypothesized that introducing increasingly bulky groups off the middle of the polymethine chain, at the 4′ position, would allow the slip angle to be modulated in a systematic manner, leading to more red-shifted emissive aggregates.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1a-1d
reference_evidence_units.statement: Steric bulk at the 4′ aryl is meant to tune the slip of J-aggregates.

reference_evidence_units.quote: We found that the unaggregated dyes all share nearly identical absorption (798 nm) and emission (∼813 nm) wavelengths (Figure 2b), as well as similar molar absorptivity (ε) and fluorescence quantum yield (ΦF) (Figure 2c), demonstrating that the different alkyl chains are not affecting the electronics of the fluorophores.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1a-1d monomers
reference_evidence_units.statement: Monomers are photophysically identical; differences arise only on aggregation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: We observe that the J1 analogues experience a redshift as the steric bulk of the monomer is increased from H (1a) to tert-butyl (1d), while the J3 analogues experience a blueshift as the steric bulk increases.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1a-1d aggregates
reference_evidence_units.statement: J-band positions shift systematically with steric bulk.

reference_evidence_units.quote: For the most common parallel orientation of dyes in a 2D sheet, we confirmed our hypothesis that increased steric bulk increases the slip angle, leading to the most redshifted benzothiazole Jaggregate to date.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1a-1d J1
reference_evidence_units.statement: Slip from 4.6 Å (1a) to 5.2 Å (1d) reproduces the J1 red shift.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In every case, the J1 mesophase displayed emission with 1b J1 having the highest quantum yield (ΦF = 0.12%) of the four J1 mesophases (Figure 7b, Table 1).
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1a-1d J1
reference_evidence_units.statement: All J1 sheets emit in the NIR/SWIR.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Overall, 1b aggregates displayed the highest fluorescence with the J2 having a ΦF = 0.05% and the J3 displaying the highest value obtained in this study of ΦF = 0.15%.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1b J2, J3
reference_evidence_units.statement: 1b gives the brightest aggregates, including the tubular J2.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The J4 aggregate for 1b as well as 1a and 1c were all nonemissive, likely due to the increased disorder allowing for more internal conversion pathways.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1a, 1b, 1c J4

reference_evidence_units.quote: The only J4 aggregate that displayed emission was from 1d, which also has the smallest FWHM of all the J4 aggregates, suggesting it is more ordered.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1d J4

reference_evidence_units.quote: Benzothiazole dye 1b is the first example of a single cyanine chromophore aggregating to form up to four distinct spectra that can be isolated at room temperature.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1b
